subject: Aligning net terms with payroll cycle & VAT responsibilities
messages:
From: Elena Kovacs <e.kovacs@cloudscale.co.uk>

Cc: Tom Reeves <tom@cloudscale.co.uk>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 12:12:00 +0100
Subject: Sync: payroll timing + net terms for Q3 billing

Hi Sofia,

Hope you're well — we're starting to lock down Q3 billing mechanics and want to make sure Redwood's invoicing cadence aligns with our payroll/finance cycles. A few specifics from our side: 

- We run payroll on the last working day of each month; we'd prefer invoice due dates to fall shortly after that so approvals and cash flow line up.
- Our AP team operates a monthly sweep; Net30 works best but we may request Net45 for larger, infrequent invoices.
- VAT handling: for UK/EU payments we need clarity on whether Redwood will issue VAT invoicing or if reverse-charge will apply; we can provide VAT registration evidence but need the exact fields you require.
- Finally, we'd like to discuss a modest credit corridor during our ramp (first 3 months) instead of a full prepayment.

Can we set expectations and have Redwood propose a concrete schedule plus any required VAT docs? Tom (cc'd) will coordinate on the accounting side.

Thanks,
Elena Kovacs
Finance Manager | CloudScale Inc

Thanks Elena — really helpful detail. High-level response and a couple of options we can operationalize quickly: 

Option A (standard, faster onboarding)
- Invoices issued on the 1st of each month for usage in the prior calendar month; payment due Net30 from invoice date.
- This aligns with your month-end payroll if CloudScale processes payments in the first week.
- Redwood will include VAT fields for our UK/EU entity; where reverse-charge applies we will leave VAT at 0% and include the reverse-charge text. We will require the VAT number and a scanned certificate for your paying entity.

Option B (temporary flexibility during ramp)
- For the first 3 billing cycles we can issue two staggered invoices per month (mid-month & month-end) with Net45 on month-end invoices to match your approval cycle.
- We can also open a credit corridor: Redwood sets an initial credit cap equivalent to 2x your expected monthly run rate; after 90 days we will reassess and can increase the cap based on actual usage and on-time payments.

Security/compliance note: for VAT-exempt/reverse-charge handling we need a completed VAT_Evidence_Template (attached) and proof of entity registration before we finalize Net45/credit corridor. If there's a delay on evidence, we can still start on Option A while your AP gathers docs.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll loop in Jonas to provide a concrete payment schedule (he handles billing cadence and credits).
- If either option looks acceptable, we can send a redlined terms proposal and DocuSign.

Attaching: Redwood_Terms_Proposal_v1.pdf (draft) and a VAT_Evidence_Template.xlsx for your AP.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Sync: payroll timing + net terms for Q3 billing

Hi Elena / Sofia — following Sofia's options, attached is a concrete payment schedule and a proposed credit corridor mechanism. Highlights:

- Proposed schedule (Payment_Schedule_v2.xlsx):
  * Invoice issued: 1st of month (usage T-1).
  * Standard due date: Net30 (due 31st).
  * If Client opts for staggered invoices during ramp, month-mid invoice due Net30 and month-end invoice due Net45.

- Credit corridor
  * Initial cap = 2x forecasted monthly spend (illustrated in sheet 2).
  * Automatic increase trigger: 3 consecutive months of on-time payments + usage within 20% of forecast.
  * If cap is hit, we will notify 10 business days before blocking new consumption; options include immediate top-up or short-term prepayment.

- Early-pay incentive: 2% discount if payment posts within 10 days of invoice (applies to invoices < £250k).

- VAT / tax handling: Redwood will clearly annotate VAT lines for our EU entity. For reverse-charge cases, please return completed VAT_Evidence_Template and a signed cover letter per invoice-entity. Until we receive evidence we will default VAT to our invoice (so AP has the line to claim).

I've uploaded the Payment_Schedule_v2.xlsx and updated the terms draft with the staggered remit option and credit corridor language. I've also started a DocuSign envelope for the payment terms so we can get an executed agreement quickly: https://www.docusign.com/CLD-2381-payment-terms

If this looks good, Sofia — shall we push the envelope to Elena and tentatively agree Option B for the first three months?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Billing Ops | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments mentioned: Payment_Schedule_v2.xlsx
